'''Paul Frank Barbara''' (April 24, 1953 – October 31, 2010) was an American chemist. His research interests focused on the understanding of the [[molecular structure]] and dynamics of complex chemical systems, including [[organic semiconductor|organic semi-conductors]] for [[photovoltaic]] applications, [[proton]] and [[electron transfer]] reactions, the hydrated electron and intermediates in the reverse transcription mechanism of [[HIV-1]]. His laboratory developed and applied novel [[ultrafast laser spectroscopy|ultrafast]] and single molecule spectroscopies to study the complexity of these chemical system.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Mossman |first=Kaspar |date=2007-11-06 |title=Profile of Paul Barbara |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=104 |issue=45 |pages=17567–17569 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0709736104 |doi-access=free |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=2077062 |pmid=17978173|bibcode=2007PNAS..10417567M }}</ref>

Paul Barbara was a full professor at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Leahy |first=Cory |date=2010-11-03 |title=Prominent Chemist Paul Barbara Dies at 57 |url=https://news.utexas.edu/2010/11/03/prominent-chemist-paul-barbara-dies-at-57/ |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=UT News |language=en-US}}</ref> He held the R.J.V. Johnson-Welch Endowed Chair in the department of chemistry and biochemistry at UT-Austin. He was also Director of UT-Austin's Center for Nano- and Molecular Science and Technology, and Senior Editor for Accounts of Chemical Research.<ref>[http://barbara.cm.utexas.edu/ Paul F. Barbara's Group Homepage]</ref>

==Education==
Paul Barbara received his bachelor's degree in 1974 at [[Hofstra University]] and completed his doctoral work in 1978 at [[Brown University]] under the supervision of Ronald G. Lawler. From 1978 to 1980 he carried out postdoctoral work at [[Bell Laboratories]] with [[Peter M. Rentzepis]] and [[Louis E. Brus]].<ref name=":1" /> He joined the faculty of the department of chemistry at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1980, achieving the rank of full professor in 1990. He moved to the University of Texas at Austin in 1998, as full professor in the department of chemistry and biochemistry until his death.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards==
Paul Barbara was named 3M-Alumni Distinguished Professor of Chemistry in 1995, elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1999.<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter B |url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120208092238/http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf |archive-date=2012-02-08 |accessdate=May 17, 2011 |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1993, a fellow of the American Association for Advancement of Science in 2004 and a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2006. Other awards include an Alfred P. [[Sloan Fellowship]] in 1983–85, a [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]] in 1984–89, a NSF Creativity Award in 1998, Inter-American Photochemical Society Award in 2002 and the 2009 [[E. Bright Wilson Award in Spectroscopy]] in 2008 from The [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>[http://pubs.acs.org/isubscribe/journals/cen/87/i02/html/8702awards1.html C&E News E. Bright Wilson Award In Spectroscopy in 2009]</ref>
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:Paul Barbara and his "Barbarians" (2003).jpg|right|thumb|250px|Barbara and his research group (2003)]] -->The Barbara research group is nicknamed the ‘[[Barbarians]]’.

==Death==
Paul Barbara died on October 31, 2010, two weeks after a [[cardiac arrest]] sent him into a coma.<ref name=":0" />

A memorial service was held on December 12, 2010, on UT campus to celebrate the life of Paul F. Barbara.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cm.utexas.edu/news/dr-paul-barbara-memorial-service |title=Dr. Paul Barbara Memorial Service |access-date=November 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101119084437/http://www.cm.utexas.edu/news/dr-paul-barbara-memorial-service |archive-date=November 19, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is survived by his wife Sharon, daughter Juliet and son Jason.
